source_checks.finding: Page confirms the Windows 11 path (Start, Settings, Apps, Default apps, search Chrome, select Google Chrome, Set default next to 'Make Google Chrome your default browser'), the note to review 'Set default file types or link types', and the note that Chrome must be installed first. Excerpt 'To make sure the change is applied to the correct file types,' is on the page. Used correctly.

Distractor. Page confirms the Windows 10 steps (Original version and Creators Update paths, 'Web browser', 'Choose an app' window). This does not apply to this user, who states Windows 11, and it is correctly unused in the target.

required_actions.action: Open Start, then Settings, then Apps, then Default apps
Search for Chrome under 'Set defaults for applications' and select Google Chrome
Select 'Set default' next to 'Make Google Chrome your default browser'
Review the list under 'Set default file types or link types' so the change covers links
Download and install Chrome first if it is not on the computer (conditional; user already uses Chrome as the link target)

source_checks.finding: Page confirms the Windows 10 steps for both versions: Original version (System, then Default apps), Creators Update (Apps, then Default apps), 'Web browser' at the bottom, and the 'Choose an app' window with Google Chrome. Excerpt 'In the "Choose an app" window, select Google Chrome' is on the page. Used correctly.
Distractor. Page confirms the Windows 11 steps and the file-type note. This does not apply to this user, who states Windows 10, and it is correctly unused in the target.

required_actions.action: Open default apps: System, then Default apps (Original version) or Apps, then Default apps (Creators Update)
Under 'Web browser' at the bottom, select the current browser
In the 'Choose an app' window, select Google Chrome
Download and install Chrome first if it is not on the computer (conditional)

source_checks.finding: Page confirms the computer steps: More, then Settings; Privacy and security, then Site Settings, then Pop-ups and redirects; find the site under 'Allowed to send pop-ups and use redirects'; More, then Block; Add under 'Not allowed to send pop-ups or use redirects' if the site is not listed; the [*.]example.com pattern. Excerpt 'By default, Google Chrome blocks pop-ups from automatically showing up on your screen.' is on the page. Used correctly.

required_actions.action: Open Chrome, then More, then Settings
Go to Privacy and security, then Site Settings, then Pop-ups and redirects
Find the site under 'Allowed to send pop-ups and use redirects', then More, then Block
If the site is not listed, Add it under 'Not allowed to send pop-ups or use redirects' using its web address

Sign out of the old phone's entry (device the user no longer owns)
Sign out of the second entry with the same device name
